newsitem.title: UK: Interconnector gas sale breaks new ground - analysts. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Interconnector gas sale breaks new ground - analysts. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]

text.p: The sale by Mobil Corp's Mobil Europe Gas Inc (MEGAS) of U.K. natural gas to a customer in the Netherlands represents an important first because the gas is going directly to an industrial end-user, analysts said on Wednesday.
MEGAS has sold 0.8 billion cubic metres (bcm) to Norsk Hydro SDB's Sluiskil plant in Southern Holland.

The company has leased space on the 235km, 40 inch Interconnector pipeline linking Bacton on the east coast of England with Zeebrugge in Belgium (corrects from Netherlands) from Amerada Hess and National Power.
"The issue is how is the gas to get there from Zeebrugge," said energy analyst Ben Hollins at consultants Wood Mackenzie.
A spokesman for Mobil said the sale will actually take place from MEGAS to Norsk Hydro at Zeebrugge, and Norsk Hydro will then transport it to their plant.
Until now, there have been four deals through the Interconnector pipeline supplying European customers, but all have been made to distributors.
The most recent was concluded on May 14, when Centrica plc contracted to sell three bcm over seven years to Germany's Thyssengas.

Analysts speculated that there would be no difficulty in Norsk Hydro having a transportation agreement with Belgian distributor Distrigaz, as the end user is not in Belgium and so would not deprive Distrigaz of a customer.
But more surprising was the agreement by Dutch distributor Gasunie to allow the gas to be sold to an end user in the Netherlands, as this could involve Gasunie in losing a customer.
"Maybe the deal shows that Gasunie accepts third party access and liberalisation is going to happen," said an analyst. "That would be a first."
MEGAS is also the first non-equity holder in the Interconnector to become a shipper.
Centrica is not an equity holder itself, and leased capacity from BG plc to conclude its deal with Thyssengas.
But a Mobil spokesman said that although Centrica has leased capacity from a shipper, it has not become one itself.
"Mobil is the first non-equity holder to become a full Interconnector shipper," he said.
Even following the MEGAS sale, only around five bcm a year, or a quarter of the pipeline's 20 bcm capacity, has been contracted for.

Analysts said recently that more sales were likely to be concluded as market liberalisation opens up access to pipelines and allow sales directly to end users. They saw Mobil's deal as an important pointer to the future.
